snippet.title: This Is Why You Dream About People You've Lost | Mel Robbins #shorts
snippet.description:
Order your copy of The Let Them Theory 👉 https://melrob.co/let-them-theory 👈 The #1 Best Selling Book of 2025 🔥 Discover how much power you truly have. It all begins with two simple words. Let Them.
—
When you dream about someone you’ve lost, it’s not random…

Dr. Rahul Jandial is a world-renowned neuroscientist and neurosurgeon who teaches you how your brain uses dreams to process grief. 

If you wake up from those dreams and wonder what it meant, or why it felt so real. It’s because tour brain isn’t just replaying memories, it’s working through the loss you’ve experienced.

When you’re awake, you might push the feeling down, stay busy, avoid going there.

But when you’re asleep, that part of your mind opens up. The emotion, the attachment, the relationship, it all comes forward in a way your waking mind doesn’t allow.

On this episode of The Mel Robbins Podcast with Dr. Rahul Jandial, you’ll learn what your dreams are really telling you, how to understand the emotional patterns behind them, and how to use them to better understand yourself.

Watch the full episode now: https://youtu.be/GIGmGupeD_I?si=zC2GW2BVEwzCvS6G

snippet.title: Dr. Luc Van Loon: Optimizing Protein Intake & Distribution for Muscle Growth
snippet.description:
Dr. Luc van Loon is a renowned figure in the realm of exercise science, particularly celebrated for his deep understanding of protein metabolism, resistance training, and the nuanced role of collagen supplements in sports nutrition. Our conversation is an in-depth discussion on optimal protein intake & distribution strategies for stimulating muscle protein synthesis.

My free omega-3 guide (the ultimate blueprint for choosing a fish oil supplement):
https://fmfomega3guide.com/

00:06:50 Protein turnover in organs (brain, liver, etc.)
00:10:10 How much protein do you really need?
00:14:58 Recommended protein intake when dieting for weight loss
00:16:15 How the body adapts to higher protein
00:19:46 Anabolic resistance

00:24:58 Gaining strength vs. muscle mass
00:29:20 Optimal protein distribution

00:48:57 How does spreading out protein intake affect hypertrophy?

00:54:58 Protein supplementation for weight loss & recomposition

01:00:14 Raw eggs vs. cooked — what's better for hypertrophy?
01:04:07 Plant vs. animal protein

01:56:53 Benefits of smaller peptides in hydrolyzed collagen
01:58:57 Collagen's impact on skin health
02:02:46 Amino acids from hydrolyzed collagen powder
02:07:30 Luc's exercise routine & diet

snippet.description:

snippet.title: Essentials: The Biology of Aggression, Mating & Arousal | Dr. David Anderson
snippet.description:
In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, my guest is Dr. David Anderson, PhD, a professor of biology at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) and an investigator at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI). We discuss the brain circuits that underlie how emotions emerge and shape behaviors, including the neural control of fear, aggression and pain. We also explore how hormones and neuromodulators influence these emotional states, and why understanding these hidden internal processes is essential for improving future mental health treatments.

Show notes: https://go.hubermanlab.com/blBjp0e

snippet.title: Why Strength Training Matters More Than You Think
snippet.description:
You can take medication for a lot of things. You can't take a pill to replace muscle.

That's why strength training is one of the best investments you can make in your future health. Muscle supports your metabolism, protects your independence, and is one of the strongest predictors of longevity.
